```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(e1071)

data <- read.csv("/home/anaconda/Desktop/HepatitisCdata.csv",
                 stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

data$Category <- as.factor(data$Category)
data$Sex <- as.factor(data$Sex)

data <- data[, !names(data) %in% "Unnamed.0"]

print(dim(data))
print(head(data))
str(data)
```

```{r}
numeric_data <- data[, sapply(data, is.numeric)]
numeric_data <- numeric_data[, !names(numeric_data) %in% "X"]

summary_statistics <- data.frame(
  Variable = names(numeric_data),
  Mean = sapply(numeric_data, mean, na.rm = TRUE),
  Median = sapply(numeric_data, median, na.rm = TRUE),
  Minimum = sapply(numeric_data, min, na.rm = TRUE),
  Maximum = sapply(numeric_data, max, na.rm = TRUE),
  Range = sapply(numeric_data, function(x) diff(range(x, na.rm = TRUE))),
  Variance = sapply(numeric_data, var, na.rm = TRUE),
  Standard_Deviation = sapply(numeric_data, sd, na.rm = TRUE),
  IQR = sapply(numeric_data, IQR, na.rm = TRUE),
  Skewness = sapply(numeric_data, e1071::skewness, na.rm = TRUE),
  Kurtosis = sapply(numeric_data, e1071::kurtosis, na.rm = TRUE)
)

summary_statistics[, -1] <- round(summary_statistics[, -1], 4)
print(summary_statistics, row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
summary_statistics <- as.data.frame(summary_statistics)
print(summary_statistics, row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
category_frequency <- table(data$Category)
category_relative_frequency <- prop.table(category_frequency)

print(category_frequency)
print(round(category_relative_frequency, 4))

par(mfrow = c(1, 2))

pie(category_frequency,
    main = "Category Distribution",
    labels = paste(names(category_frequency),
                   round(100 * category_relative_frequency, 1), "%"))

barplot(category_frequency,
        main = "Category Frequency",
        xlab = "Category",
        ylab = "Frequency",
        las = 2)

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

```{r}
age <- data$Age

age_breaks <- seq(
  floor(min(age, na.rm = TRUE)),
  ceiling(max(age, na.rm = TRUE)) + 10,
  by = 10
)

age_breaks <- sort(unique(c(age_breaks, max(age, na.rm = TRUE) + 1)))
age_bins <- cut(age, breaks = age_breaks, right = FALSE, include.lowest = TRUE)

age_frequency <- table(age_bins)
print(age_frequency)

par(mfrow = c(1, 2))

hist(age,
     breaks = age_breaks,
     main = "Age Histogram",
     xlab = "Age",
     ylab = "Frequency")

boxplot(age,
        main = "Age Box Plot",
        ylab = "Age")

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

```{r}
contingency_table <- table(data$Category, data$Sex)

print(contingency_table)
print(round(prop.table(contingency_table, margin = 1), 4))
print(round(prop.table(contingency_table, margin = 2), 4))
print(round(prop.table(contingency_table), 4))
```

```{r}
barplot(contingency_table,
        beside = FALSE,
        main = "Category and Sex - Stacked Bar Plot",
        xlab = "Category",
        ylab = "Frequency",
        legend.text = TRUE,
        las = 2)
```

```{r}
grouped_statistics <- aggregate(
  ALT ~ Category,
  data = data,
  FUN = function(x) c(
    Mean = mean(x, na.rm = TRUE),
    Median = median(x, na.rm = TRUE),
    Standard_Deviation = sd(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
)

grouped_statistics <- data.frame(
  Category = grouped_statistics$Category,
  Mean = grouped_statistics$ALT[, "Mean"],
  Median = grouped_statistics$ALT[, "Median"],
  Standard_Deviation = grouped_statistics$ALT[, "Standard_Deviation"]
)

grouped_statistics[, -1] <- round(grouped_statistics[, -1], 4)
print(grouped_statistics, row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
boxplot(ALT ~ Category,
        data = data,
        main = "ALT Distribution Across Categories",
        xlab = "Category",
        ylab = "ALT",
        las = 2)

ggplot(data, aes(x = Category, y = ALT)) +
  geom_violin(trim = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "ALT Violin Plot Across Categories",
       x = "Category",
       y = "ALT") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

```{r}
pearson_correlation <- cor(data$ALT, data$AST,
                           use = "complete.obs",
                           method = "pearson")

spearman_correlation <- cor(data$ALT, data$AST,
                            use = "complete.obs",
                            method = "spearman")

print(pearson_correlation)
print(spearman_correlation)

plot(data$ALT, data$AST,
     main = "ALT vs AST",
     xlab = "ALT",
     ylab = "AST",
     pch = 19)

abline(lm(AST ~ ALT, data = data), lwd = 2)
```

```{r}
combination_statistics <- aggregate(
  ALT ~ Category + Sex,
  data = data,
  FUN = function(x) c(
    Mean = mean(x, na.rm = TRUE),
    Standard_Deviation = sd(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
)

combination_statistics <- data.frame(
  Category = combination_statistics$Category,
  Sex = combination_statistics$Sex,
  Mean = combination_statistics$ALT[, "Mean"],
  Standard_Deviation = combination_statistics$ALT[, "Standard_Deviation"]
)

combination_statistics[, 3:4] <- round(combination_statistics[, 3:4], 4)
print(combination_statistics, row.names = FALSE)

ggplot(data, aes(x = Sex, y = ALT)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  facet_wrap(~ Category) +
  labs(title = "Faceted Box Plot of ALT by Category and Sex",
       x = "Sex",
       y = "ALT") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

ggplot(combination_statistics, aes(x = Category, y = Mean, fill = Sex)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.9)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = Mean - Standard_Deviation,
                    ymax = Mean + Standard_Deviation),
                position = position_dodge(width = 0.9),
                width = 0.2) +
  labs(title = "Mean ALT with Standard Deviation Error Bars",
       x = "Category",
       y = "Mean ALT") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

```{r}
ggplot(data, aes(x = ALT, y = AST, color = Sex, shape = Sex)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "ALT vs AST by Sex",
       x = "ALT",
       y = "AST")

for (level in levels(data$Sex)) {
  subset_data <- data[data$Sex == level, c("ALT", "AST")]

  correlation_matrix <- cor(subset_data,
                            use = "complete.obs",
                            method = "pearson")

  cat("\nCorrelation Matrix for Sex:", level, "\n")
  print(round(correlation_matrix, 4))
}
```

```{r}
selected_numeric <- data[, c("ALB", "ALT", "AST", "BIL", "CHE")]

correlation_matrix <- cor(selected_numeric,
                          use = "complete.obs",
                          method = "pearson")

print(round(correlation_matrix, 4))

heatmap(correlation_matrix,
        Rowv = NA,
        Colv = NA,
        scale = "none",
        main = "Correlation Matrix Heatmap",
        margins = c(8, 8))
```
